Clean up coreboot-utils and change it to be pulled in by userfeedback sys-apps/coreboot-utils serves two purposes: with cros_host it installs several utilities that are needed to build a firmware image, and for an actual board it installs the cbmem utility that is used to query runtime firmware information (e.g. for chrome://system). (It also installs cbfstool for a factory use case that should probably be solved by supplying it externally instead, but that is out of scope for this bug... see crosbug.com/p/49634.) However, the dependencies that pull coreboot-utils in are very weird: the cros_host use case is solved by build-time DEPENDs from the various firmware ebuilds, which works fine... but on base images it seems that it only gets installed as an RDEPEND of the depthcharge ebuild that should've really been a DEPEND anyway. The problem is that the depthcharge ebuild doesn't always get emerged on system images, because it depends on the USE=bootimage flag. This is only set for a few boards that we explicitly selected to continue building ToT firmware for the CQ, whereas the actual firmware running on Chromebooks comes from firmware branches. (The chipset-skylake-private overlay also has a custom dependency on coreboot-utils, presumably to get it to appear on some boards that didn't have USE=bootimage set on ToT.) This patch fixes this weirdness by pulling coreboot-utils in from the userfeedback ebuild instead, which contains the code that actually calls these utilities. Also add it unconditionally to developer images just in case. Fix up depthcharge's dependencies and make a few of the installed utilities conditional to cros_host which aren't really needed outside the build process. Removing the sys-apps/pciutils dependency because I have no idea how it got there in the first place. I don't know of anything in coreboot-utils that would require it at runtime. If people want it available for testing purposes, it still gets pulled in directly by chromium-os-test. Removing the old USE=coreboot flag from all remaining packages while I'm here... this flag was only used to differentiate coreboot systems from legacy EFI firmware many years ago, and has become vestigal with recent firmware build refactorings. FROMLIST: x86/mm/kaslr: Use the _ASM_MUL macro for multiplication to work around Clang incompatibility The constraint "rm" allows the compiler to put mix_const into memory. When the input operand is a memory location then MUL needs an operand size suffix, since Clang can't infer the multiplication width from the operand. Add and use the _ASM_MUL macro which determines the operand size and resolves to the NUL instruction with the corresponding suffix. This fixes the following error when building with clang: CC arch/x86/lib/kaslr.o /tmp/kaslr-dfe1ad.s: Assembler messages: /tmp/kaslr-dfe1ad.s:182: Error: no instruction mnemonic suffix given and no register operands; can't size instruction Link: https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/9707283/ (Applied to git.kernel.org tip/tip master) BUG=chromium:702746 TEST=build for edgar Signed-off-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Cc: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org> Cc: Greg Hackmann <ghackmann@google.com> Cc: Kees Cook <keescook@chromium.org> Cc: Linus Torvalds <torvalds@linux-foundation.org> Cc: Michael Davidson <md@google.com> Cc: Peter Zijlstra <peterz@infradead.org> Cc: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de> Link: http://lkml.kernel.org/r/20170501224741.133938-1-mka@chromium.org Signed-off-by: Ingo Molnar <mingo@kernel.org> Change-Id: I8342359e0866ccfb970a443d7a6f450d6a272e7d Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/497589 Commit-Ready: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Tested-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: AF_VSOCK: Shrink the area influenced by prepare_to_wait When a thread is prepared for waiting by calling prepare_to_wait, sleeping is not allowed until either the wait has taken place or finish_wait has been called. The existing code in af_vsock imposed unnecessary no-sleep assumptions to a broad list of backend functions. This patch shrinks the influence of prepare_to_wait to the area where it is strictly needed, therefore relaxing the no-sleep restriction there.
